items.title: Pressure ramps up on Le Bris as Sunderland beaten by Dinamo Zagreb
items.excerpt: Pressure is ramping up even more on Regis Le Bris as Sunderland were comfortably beaten 2-0 by Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League to continue the Black Cats' torrid run of form.
body: Pressure is ramping up even more on Regis Le Bris as Sunderland were comfortably beaten 2-0 by Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League to continue the Black Cats' torrid run of form.
Before the game, Le Bris said Sunderland have been too exposed and leaky in defence - but his team were not listening as they went in 2-0 down at half-time in front of an angry Stadium of Light.

Poor marking from a corner allowed Luka Stojkovic to volley in the first goal - then the Dinamo midfielder set up Dion Beljo with a delightful chipped pass, with his deft finish equally sweet, although the red and white defenders were all at sea in the move.

At the other end of the pitch, Sunderland were a little more unfortunate. They struck the woodwork in both halves through defenders Thomas Meunier and Kevin Danso. Heroic defending from Dinamo also denied Malick Fofana and Trai Hume in the same move with last-ditch blocks.

Palmer was hugely disappointed when he was overlooked for the World Cup in the summer after a stop-start season due to injury, and he withdrew from the last England camp in September and October because of a minor fitness issue.

The 24-year-old has been unavailable for selection due to injury three times since Tuchel took over, and he has withdrawn from two further squads after being named. He has only played three times for his country since the German coach took the reins in January 2025.

body: Oliver Glasner says he meant for his post-Brentford outburst to be positive and a catalyst for change at Nottingham Forest.
The head coach went on two explosive rants to Sky Sports and in his post-match press conference after defeat at the Gtech Community Stadium which left Forest 19th in the league.

Among other things, Glasner said: "We have to accept it's not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do.

"I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises. It's a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in." body: Gianni Infantino is facing his first serious challenger for the FIFA presidency after Japanese football chief Kohzo Tashima announced his intention to stand in March's election.

Tashima, a member of the FIFA Council and honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), will have the backing of his national association and is expected to secure the five endorsements required to become an official candidate.

items.title: Trophies, tears, records and rows - Ronaldo's Portugal career will divide opinion
items.excerpt: Trophies, tears, records and rows, Cristiano Ronaldo's international career had it all.
body: Trophies, tears, records and rows, Cristiano Ronaldo's international career had it all.
For 23 years he passionately wore the Portugal shirt. The debates about his achievements and legacy representing his country will go on for even longer.
They will primarily focus on two questions. In his pomp, should he have lifted Portugal to greater heights? And in his final years, did he hold the team back from their full potential?

What shouldn't be lost in the analysis - when Ronaldo's record will inevitably be weighed up against that of his great rival (and World Cup winner) Lionel Messi - is that across his unmatched 234 caps, Ronaldo's brilliance helped deliver glory days.

items.title: Southampton hit back to hold West Brom
items.excerpt: Samuel Edozie's second-half equaliser ensured Southampton and West Brom shared the points from a 1-1 draw at The Hawthorns.
body: Samuel Edozie's second-half equaliser ensured Southampton and West Brom shared the points from a 1-1 draw at The Hawthorns.
Both teams started the season in promising fashion and taking a point apiece means the sides continue their respective unbeaten runs after a game of two halves.

West Brom completely dominated the first half as Southampton failed to register a single shot in the opening 45 and Isaac Price notched from the penalty spot to give the hosts a deserved half-time lead for his fifth goal of the season.
For all the hosts' dominance, Tonda Eckert's side turned the tables in the second period and found an equaliser through Edozie.
